key_insight: Ceramic performance is controlled by the coupled chain from atomic bonding and processing to microstructure, which ultimately governs mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biomedical properties.
engineering_relevance: Designing ceramics means balancing densification, defects, porosity, grain size, and phase stability to achieve reliable parts for structural, electronic, and biomedical applications.
method: Compare sintering, sol–gel, and additive manufacturing
Survey biomedical ceramics and emerging design directions
evidence_signal: The paper is a narrative review synthesizing reported relationships across ceramic systems rather than presenting new experimental data or a single benchmark evaluation.
watch_item: A major implementation challenge is the brittleness and porosity–strength trade-off, which can be amplified by processing heterogeneity, residual stress, and scale-up issues.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
